# Intake Brief: Ship skill invalidates audits

## Problem statement

Running `/skill:ship` leaves many work items reading as having an **out-of-date
("invalidated") audit**. The release close path writes to every item it
releases — `wl close --force --reason "Shipped in vX"` and
`wl update --status completed --stage done` (plus comments) — which bumps each
item's `updatedAt` well after its `auditedAt`. The freshness **time gate**
(`isAuditStale` in `skill/ship/scripts/audit-freshness.js`, mirrored by
`_check_audit_freshness` in `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`) treats
`auditedAt < updatedAt − 60 s` (outside the 30 s persistence-write tolerance)
as stale. Only audits that carry a **v2 content fingerprint**
(`Audit content fingerprint (v2): …`) are immune, because the content-freshness
probe can confirm the item's title/description did not change; legacy/manual
audits (no v2 line) fall all the way back to the time gate and therefore
genuinely read as invalidated. Time-based consumers (e.g. the herdr
dispatcher's `isAuditFresh`) flag all of them.

## Users

- **Producers running a release** — user story: "When I run `/skill:ship` I
  don't want the audit panel to light up with 'out of date' on dozens of just-
  released items, forcing me to re-audit finished work just to clear the
  flags."
- **Audit operators / automated dispatchers** — user story: "I want audit
  freshness to reflect whether the audited content actually changed, not
  whether an unrelated lifecycle write (close, stage/status transition, sync)
  touched `updatedAt`."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **RCA documented.** Identify the exact ship/release steps that move
   `updatedAt` on released items and the exact freshness rule that then reports
   them stale, with representative item ids and timestamps as evidence (e.g.
   audited `2026-11-15T12:20:27Z`, re-staged to completed `12:27:05Z`, closed
   by ship `14:17:53Z`). Classify the affected audits: v2 content-fresh
   (protected by the probe) versus legacy/manual (time-gate only).
2. **Decision recorded — intended or avoidable.** State, with justification
   tied to the existing content-freshness contract, whether the invalidation is
   an intended side effect of the release writes or an avoidable defect, and
   which layer is at fault (release write path, freshness rule, or a display/
   dispatcher consumer).
3. **Fix if avoidable.** Implement the minimal change so that a ship run does
   not leave content-unchanged audits reading as out of date — for example,
   preserving the audit freshness signal through the close/re-stage write (a
   content fingerprint of the final description, or not bumping the audited
   timestamp semantics) — **without** re-running the expensive audit pipeline
   for the backlog and without weakening verdict semantics.
4. **Explain if intended.** If (and only if) the RCA proves the behaviour is
   intended, add the missing explanation to the affected work item and docs so
   the side effect and its rationale are recorded — including any display-only
   consumer (herdr) that should be scoped out with a linked item.
5. **Targeted tests.** Add or extend tests that lock the chosen behaviour:
   a lifecycle-only `updatedAt` bump after a v2 audit still reports fresh; a
   content (title/description) change still invalidates; and the legacy/manual
   fallback behaves as documented. Tests must exercise production code, not
   re-implement it.
6. **Documentation updated.** Update `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`,
   `skill/audit/SKILL.md` and `skill/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md`
   (plus any relevant wiki/docs-site entry) to reflect the change or decision.
7. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Impact

After a release, producers stop seeing content-unchanged work items flagged as
"audit out of date", so they no longer have to re-audit finished work just to
clear spurious staleness.

## Constraints

- **Verdict semantics unchanged:** freshness only decides when an audit is
  reused or how staleness is displayed; it never changes what an audit
  concludes. `--force` still bypasses the gate.
- **No mass re-audit:** any fix must not fan out the full audit pipeline across
  the in-review/backlog set; the content-freshness fast path and bounded
  remediation must keep their cost profile.
- **Read-only probes stay read-only:** no test-suite execution or pi calls from
  the freshness probe.
- **Preserve the existing content-fresh fast path** (`hasContentFingerprint` /
  `queryContentFreshness` / `attemptAuditRemediation`) and child-reuse gate.
- **Repository boundary:** the herdr/ContextHub dispatcher (`isAuditFresh` in
  `packages/herdr/src/icons.ts`) is a different repository; if the RCA shows a
  change there is required, file a linked item rather than editing it here.

## Existing state

- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` — release close path. Around lines
  700–735 it invokes `wl close <id> --force --reason "Shipped in vX"`,
  `wl update <child> --status completed --stage done`, and `wl comment add`.
  Each write bumps `updatedAt`; none changes the item's title or description.
- `skill/ship/scripts/audit-freshness.js` — `isAuditStale()` is the shared
  time gate. An audit is fresh only when `auditedAt > updatedAt + 60 s`, or
  when `updatedAt` is 0–30 s after `auditedAt` (the audit's own persistence
  write). Everything else is stale.
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js` — `getAuditStatus()` reports
  `stale` for a passing-but-time-stale audit; `hasContentFingerprint()` only
  matches the **v2** line; `queryContentFreshness()` calls
  `audit_runner.py check-freshness <id> --json`, which resolves a time-stale
  audit as fresh when the v2 fingerprint still matches. Legacy/unversioned
  fingerprints are deliberately not matched and fall back to the time gate.
- `skill/ship/scripts/refresh-audits.js` — `planAuditRefresh()` classifies a
  passing-but-time-stale audit as `toRefresh` (it consults the time gate, not
  the content probe), so ship pre-flight can plan re-audits of content-fresh
  items; the runner then short-circuits, but the stored `auditedAt` is not
  re-stamped, so a time-based consumer keeps seeing it as out of date.
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_check_audit_freshness()` (~line
  2380) is the authoritative freshness gate (v2 content gate, then 60 s time
  gate with the 30 s persistence tolerance). On a content-fresh short-circuit
  it returns the stored report **without** re-stamping `auditedAt`.
  `AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_PREFIX` (~line 1434) is
  `"Audit content fingerprint (v2): "`; `_compute_content_fingerprint()` (~line
  3111) hashes `{schema: 2, title_hash, description_hash}` with zero git calls.
- `skill/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` — documents the
  content-freshness contract: "content-fresh audits are trusted regardless of
  `updatedAt` … a `wl sync`-moved `updatedAt` can never force a re-audit of
  unchanged content" (Step 2 audit gate section, ~lines 200–232).
- **Observed evidence (current store):** of 1 685 audited, non-deleted items,
  1 274 are time-stale and 1 272 of those are completed; **1 155** of the stale
  audits carry no v2 fingerprint line (legacy or manual "Approved by manual
  review" audits), and 119 stale audits do carry a v2 line (content changed
  after the audit). Example `SA-0MWE1EAR30045VHO`: audited
  `2026-11-15T12:20:27Z`, cascaded to completed `12:27:05Z`, closed by ship
  `14:17:53Z`; `check-freshness` still reports **fresh** (v2 content match)
  even though the time gate calls it stale. Example `SA-0MWE4BT63005N8OE`:
  manual audit (`rawOutput` empty, summary "Approved by manual review"),
  audited `2026-11-13T22:46:08Z`, closed by ship `2026-11-15T14:17:46Z`;
  `check-freshness` reports **stale (legacy audit, time gate)**.
- **Discovered-from observation (out of scope here):** release close comments
  read `Shipped in vv0.1.28` (double `v`). Track separately if it is not
  already known.

## Desired change

Run the RCA above, then apply the smallest change that makes the outcome match
the producer's expectation: a ship run must not mark content-unchanged audits
as out of date. Prefer fixing the **release write / freshness-signal** path
(e.g. preserving or re-deriving a truthful content fingerprint for the final
description on close, so content-freshness resolves) over changing the audit
verdict or fanning out re-audits. If the RCA proves the behaviour is an
intended, unavoidable consequence of the time gate, record the explanation and
the rationale in the work item and docs instead, and file a linked item for any
display-only consumer that should change.

## Key Files

- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` — release close path (`wl close`,
  `wl update --status completed --stage done`, `wl comment add`); likely site
  for avoiding an unnecessary freshness-signal bump.
- `skill/ship/scripts/audit-freshness.js` — `isAuditStale()` time gate.
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js` — `getAuditStatus()`,
  `hasContentFingerprint()`, `queryContentFreshness()`,
  `attemptAuditRemediation()`.
- `skill/ship/scripts/refresh-audits.js` — `planAuditRefresh()` (time-gate
  classification; whether to consult content freshness at plan time).
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_check_audit_freshness()`,
  `_compute_content_fingerprint()`, `_extract_content_fingerprint()`,
  `AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_PREFIX`, `AUDIT_PERSIST_WRITE_TOLERANCE_SECONDS`,
  persistence path (`persist_audit`).
- `skill/ship/tests/` and `skill/audit/tests/` — freshness/gate test coverage.
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`, `skill/audit/SKILL.md`,
  `skill/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` — freshness-gate docs.

## Related work

- **SA-0MSRVI17W004U9G0** — Simplify audit freshness: invalidate only on this
  work item's own data change (completed, shipped v0.1.24). Introduced the
  item-data-only v2 fingerprint and the legacy time-gate fallback this item
  observes.
- **SA-0MUOO5TRU005ALBL** — Ship skill: eliminate stale-audit false blocks and
  bound release-time audit cost (completed). Added the content-fresh fast path
  so content-unchanged audits are not re-audited by the release gates.
- **SA-0MUOO5W8J001DYTI** — Ship: consume persisted audit content fingerprint
  (completed). Added `queryContentFreshness()` / `check-freshness` probe.
- **SA-0MVTU2643004QTQN** — Content-freshness contract: content-fresh audits
  are trusted regardless of `updatedAt` (completed).
- **SA-0MVAWFJXM0096FAB**, **SA-0MVAWFYKT002CQ3L** — child freshness
  fingerprint test coverage / stabilisation (completed).
- **SA-0MPE03RD0005NE0H** — ralph: skip redundant start-of-iteration audit
  when the persisted audit is up to date (completed) — adjacent freshness
  consumer.
- **WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT** (ContextHub worklog) — RCA: downtime dispatcher
  re-dispatches the same item; the herdr `isAuditFresh` time-based trigger is a
  separate repository concern, out of scope unless the RCA proves otherwise.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — "invalidated (out of date)" means the freshness signal, not a
  destroyed audit record.** Stored audits remain retrievable; the item is marked
  stale by the time gate / a consumer. If the producer means audits are being
  *deleted* or overwritten, re-scope.
- **Assumption — the release close path is the dominant trigger.** The observed
  evidence points at `wl close`/`wl update --status completed` bumping
  `updatedAt` after the audit; `wl sync` re-sort is a secondary candidate to
  confirm during the RCA.
- **Risk — fabricated audit metadata.** Writing a content fingerprint at close
  must not imply a new audit verdict. Preserve the original `auditedAt` and
  verdict; only record the content hash if that is truthful.
- **Risk — scope creep into herdr.** The dispatcher is a different repository;
  link rather than edit.
- **Risk — mass re-audit / cost blow-up.** Any "fix" that re-audits the backlog
  is unacceptable; the content-fresh fast path must remain.
- **Risk — regressing the block-prevention fix.** SA-0MUOO5TRU005ALBL's stale-
  audit false-block remedy must keep working.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- **OPEN QUESTION (scope):** Does "audits invalidated (out of date)" refer to
  (a) the audit-freshness *signal* shown by consumers (herdr icon, `wl`
  display) treating a content-unchanged audit as stale, or (b) an actual loss/
  overwrite of stored audit records? — **Assumption (Map, intake):** (a). The
  store inspection shows audits present and retrievable, with staleness driven
  by `updatedAt` moving after `auditedAt`. Source: `.worklog/worklog.db`
  `audit_results` scan (1 685 audited items; 1 274 time-stale; 1 155 without a
  v2 line).
- **OPEN QUESTION (layer):** If the cause is the time gate, which layer should
  change — the release write path (avoid the unnecessary `updatedAt` bump /
  preserve the freshness signal), the freshness rule, or the display consumer
  (herdr, separate repo)? — **Assumption (Map, intake):** prefer the release
  write path or a truthful content-fingerprint preservation; keep herdr out of
  scope with a linked item. Source: RCA hypothesis, not yet producer-confirmed.
- **OPEN QUESTION (fix vs explain):** The brief is structured as
  "RCA, then fix if avoidable, else explain". If the producer already knows
  this is intended, the fix ACs can be dropped. — **Assumption (Map, intake):**
  run the RCA first; do not assume intent. Source: item seed wording ("Is this
  an intended side-effect … or … avoided").

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MPE03RD0005NE0H** – ralph: skip redundant start-of-iteration audit when persisted audit is up-to-date (completed)
- **SA-0MW0LP0OZ009OTR9** – Docs: document slot discovery, effective ceiling and slot_busy (completed)
- **SA-0MLYEOJ2N0UC3XCY** – Refactor tests for descriptor-driven audit API (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: audits, date, effect, explain, fix (+12 more)
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — matched: audits, date, effect, explain, fix (+11 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: audits, date, effect, explain, fix, former (+10 more)


---

## Plan: changelog

- **2026-11-16** — `/skill:plan SA-0MVX4EHUP0042V9G` (downtime-dispatched, herdr-downtime).
  - Pre-check: effort Small / risk Medium → full planning (above the skip threshold); plan-approval gate: not required.
  - Decomposed into 5 children (test-first dependency order):
    - SA-0MWJ4TIJT004NFJN — RCA: ship writes that invalidate audits (feature)
    - SA-0MWJ4TL8N006LYF9 — Freshness regression tests (task) — depends on F1
    - SA-0MWJ4TOMX003BZ6K — Stop ship invalidating unchanged audits (feature) — depends on F2 + F1
    - SA-0MWJ4TPHS008NOTN — Freshness documentation update (docs) — depends on F3
    - SA-0MWJ4TQMH0047HH9 — Full project suite passes (task) — depends on F3 + F4
  - Six automated review stages run on the plan (see session report): no intent-altering changes required; four redundant auto-close placeholder children were deleted after the planned children were strengthened to cover parent ACs 1/5/6/7 directly (AC coverage review: proceed, 100%).
  - Effort/risk refreshed from child aggregation: Small / Medium (score 6).

# Release gate (merge-dev-to-main.sh) discards the runner JSON, so a dev→main release cannot say why the suite gate failed

Discovered-from: **SA-0MVSJX5HS002JDHI** (during `/skill:plan`).

## Problem statement

`skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` runs the full-suite release
gate as:

```bash
if python3 "$TEST_RUNNER" --scope full --strict-git-env 2>&1; then
```

The runner's machine-readable result is never requested and the exit code is
the only signal, so a slot-contention expiry (`slot_busy`), a killed suite
(`killed`) and a genuine red suite all produce the same message: "Full test
suite failed on the merged dev→main tree — the release is blocked." The
operator cannot tell "fix the code" from "wait for a slot / raise
`TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT`", and a release attempt can burn hours of queue wait before
failing indistinguishably from a real regression.

The pre-push hook gets the equivalent fix under **SA-0MVSJX5HS002JDHI** (its
AC2/AC3); this item is the same defect on the release path.

## Users

- **Release operator** — *"As the release operator running `run-release.js`, I need the merge gate to tell me whether the suite is red, the slot pool is saturated, or the run was killed, so I can decide fix-vs-retry."*
- **Agent driving a release** — *"As the agent, I need the release gate to emit the same `gate_reason=<code>` vocabulary the pre-push hook uses, so I can act on the diagnostic instead of blindly re-running."*

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Consumes runner JSON and reports `gate_reason=<code>`.** The release gate runs `run_tests.py --json --scope full --strict-git-env`, captures stdout to a temp file, and classifies the result through the shared `gate_reason` classifier (repo-local tier first, then `~/.pi/agent/skills/test/scripts/`). On failure it prints a `gate_reason=<code>` line and a human-readable diagnostic from `render_gate_diagnostic()`.
- **AC2 — Distinct messages for contention/killed vs red suite.** A slot-contention or killed-run failure prints a distinct message with the remediation hint (wait then re-run, or raise `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT`), while a red suite keeps the "Full test suite failed" message with its own remediation.
- **AC3 — Fails closed in every failure case; `SHIP_TEST_SKIP=1` still bypasses.** The gate exits non-zero on every failure path (slot contention, timeout, killed, test failure, unparsed, infrastructure, unknown). `SHIP_TEST_SKIP=1` bypasses the gate entirely, as it does today.
- **AC4 — Hermetic test pins the classification.** A test in `tests/test_release_full_suite_gate.py` (or a new test file) exercises the classifier against a fake runner that produces JSON results for slot contention, killed, and red-suite cases, asserting the correct `gate_reason` and diagnostic output.

## Impact

The release gate now tells operators exactly why a dev→main release is blocked, so they can fix code versus retry infrastructure waits instead of blindly re-running.

## Constraints

- Reuse the shared classifier (`gate_reason.py` — `classify_gate_result`, `render_gate_diagnostic`) from the test skill; do not duplicate classification logic.
- Follow the pre-push hook's pattern: run with `--json`, capture stdout, classify via inline Python.
- UK English throughout.
- The gate must remain hermetically testable (the existing test fixture pattern must continue to work).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — scope creep**: expanding the release gate to add new classification logic beyond display would duplicate the classifier. Mitigation: consume `gate_reason.py` only; record extra opportunities as linked work items.
- **Risk — classifier availability**: a partial install lacking `gate_reason.py` must fall back to a conservative `gate_reason=infrastructure` message, never fail open.
- **Assumption**: the shared classifier is importable via the same tiered search (repo-local `skill/test/scripts/`, then `~/.pi/agent/skills/test/scripts/`) the pre-push hook uses.
- **Assumption**: the existing fake runner in the test fixture only records invocations and returns an exit code; the new tests add JSON-emitting variants without breaking the green/red/bypass cases.

## Key Files

- `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` — The release gate must be modified to capture JSON and classify failures.
- `skill/test/scripts/gate_reason.py` — Shared classifier (read-only dependency).
- `tests/test_release_full_suite_gate.py` — Existing tests; new classification tests go here.

## Related work

- **SA-0MVSJX5HS002JDHI** — Pre-push hook fix that introduces the shared classifier and applies it to the dev-push gate. Completed.
- **SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81** — Original release gate implementation (green-only gate).
- **SA-0MQAUIMBT009351X** – Post-release dev sync: return to dev and merge main after ship (completed)
- **SA-0MR3P8N3V001Q3RG** – Add rebuild step to implement SKILL.md after git pull (completed)
- **SA-0MPU0BSJ5003OTO7** – Update implement skill for dev-first workflow (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — matched: ac2, ac3, acceptance, attempt, bash (+106 more)
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: ac2, ac3, acceptance, attempt, bash (+103 more)
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — matched: ac2, ac3, acceptance, attempt, bash (+102 more)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions needed — the work item is sufficiently defined. The implementation pattern is clear from the pre-push hook fix (SA-0MVSJX5HS002JDHI), and the acceptance criteria map directly to the required changes.

## Goal

As a producer/agent, I want a single, reproducible per-test-file **keep / rework / prune** verdict that combines churn, mutation, anti-pattern and runtime evidence, so test-value decisions are made from one reconciled report rather than four separate reads.

## Problem statement

Today the evidence for test value is fragmented across `skill/test-churn`
(evolution/growth), the mutation-testing campaign (`SA-0MV28WY5Q003N54O`, fault
detection), `evaluate_usefulness.py` + `test-writing-guidelines.md` (static
anti-patterns) and the test runner (runtime/flake). Each answers a different
question; none produces an auditable per-file verdict. Epic `SA-0MVSGIMHK004QHOO`
needs a repeatable classify → prove → report pipeline, and this skill is the
missing connective tissue between those signals.

## Users

- **Producer / engineering manager** — wants a per-file keep/rework/prune
  register with the evidence for each verdict, so test-value decisions are
  auditable from one artefact instead of four tool reads.
- **Agent working the test-value epic** — wants one documented command and
  machine-readable output to drive the classify/prove/report phases without
  re-deriving verdicts by hand.
- **Maintainer of the agent infrastructure** — wants the aggregator pinned,
  deterministic and read-only so it can be rerun and compared over time.

Example user stories:

- As a producer, I want every in-scope test file to carry a keep/rework/prune
  verdict with its evidence, so I can review test value in one pass.
- As an agent, I want the aggregator to consume the existing churn, mutation and
  anti-pattern outputs rather than recompute them, so runs stay consistent with
  those tools.
- As a maintainer, I want the report to state which signals were absent, so a
  partial run never masquerades as a complete verdict.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Ingests, per test file: churn metrics (rewrite/growth/stability), mutation score, anti-pattern verdicts, and runtime/flake data when available.
- [ ] Emits one verdict per file — `keep`, `rework` or `prune` — with the evidence for that verdict recorded.
- [ ] Totals reconcile: verdict counts sum to files in scope, and every verdict cites at least one evidence source.
- [ ] Produces `test_value_report.md` + `test_value_data.json` with documented definitions and limitations.
- [ ] Orchestrates the existing analysers; it does not reimplement churn, mutation or anti-pattern detection.
- [ ] Missing inputs degrade honestly (the report states which signals were absent; it never fabricates a verdict).
- [ ] Reproducible (pinned inputs, documented command, deterministic ordering) and covered by tests.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A producer or agent can open one reconciled report and see, for every test file, whether to keep, rework or prune it — with the evidence cited — instead of manually cross-reading four separate analysers.

## Constraints

- Read-only against the analysed project.
- Must not turn a heuristic into an automatic deletion; `prune` is advisory and conservative.
- No per-project hardcoded paths; project root is an argument.
- Follows the repository skill contract and `$(skill_path ...)` shared-library resolution.
- Consumes upstream analyser outputs as inputs; must not duplicate their logic. Where an upstream signal is missing, record it as absent rather than infer it.
- Deterministic ordering and pinned input versions so two runs on the same inputs produce byte-identical verdicts (modulo reported timestamps).
- The verdict model must be documented (signal weights/thresholds and the conservative decision rules) and covered by unit tests, including the "all signals absent" and contradictory-signal cases.
- `prune` never deletes anything itself — it is a recommendation only; removal remains a separate, evidence-backed action.

## Existing state

- `skill/test-churn/scripts/test_churn_analysis.py` produces `test_churn_data.json`
  + `test_churn_report.md` (per-file churn, growth, rewrite/stability). Run as of
  writing: net growth dominated by additive accumulation, low rewrite ratio.
- The mutation arm (`SA-0MV28WY5Q003N54O`) will add `skill/mutation-test/` producing
  a per-module mutation score and a `suite_source_map.json` mapping test suites to
  the source modules they exercise. It is planned, not yet landed.
- `skill/test/scripts/evaluate_usefulness.py` produces a per-file static
  anti-pattern verdict (`keep` / `remove` / `report-to-user`) with reasons.
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` records suite wall-clock (`elapsed_seconds`);
  per-test runtime/flakiness is tracked separately (`SA-0MVXVC9FM003ZJKJ`) and may
  be absent.
- Epic `SA-0MVSGIMHK004QHOO` defines the classify/prove/report pipeline this skill
  serves; its Classify/Prove children need a per-file reconciled register.

## Desired change

- Add a `skill/test-value/` skill with a documented SKILL.md (purpose, when to
  use, workflow, outputs, limitations) and a single entry point that:
  1. Resolves the project root and the set of in-scope test files.
  2. Loads each available signal: churn JSON, mutation JSON, anti-pattern verdicts,
     optional runtime/flake data.
  3. Reconciles them into one of `keep` / `rework` / `prune` per file using a
     documented, conservative decision model, recording each contributing signal
     (or its absence) as evidence.
  4. Emits `test_value_report.md` (human) and `test_value_data.json`
     (machine-readable), with a reconciled totals section and a limitations note
     listing every absent signal.
- Provide unit tests for the verdict decision model (including absent-signal,
  conflict and all-signals-present cases), input loading (each analyser's JSON,
  and missing/malformed files), deterministic ordering, and the two output
  artefacts.
- Add tests that prove the aggregator orchestrates rather than reimplements:
  a test that feeds synthetic upstream JSON and asserts the aggregator does not
  recompute churn/anti-pattern metrics itself.
- Document the definitions, the decision model and the known limitations (e.g.
  mutation score is per-module, so per-file attribution follows the suite→source
  map and is approximate; runtime may be absent).

## Key Files

- `skill/test-value/SKILL.md` — Skill contract: purpose, when-to-use, workflow, outputs, limitations, decision model.
- `skill/test-value/scripts/aggregate_test_value.py` — Entry point: resolve inputs, reconcile signals, emit report + JSON.
- `skill/test-value/scripts/decision_model.py` — Documented, unit-testable keep/rework/prune reconciliation rules.
- `skill/test-value/scripts/loaders.py` — Adapters that read each upstream analyser's JSON and record absent/malformed signals.
- `skill/test-value/tests/test_decision_model.py` — Verdict rules incl. absent-signal, conflict, all-present cases.
- `skill/test-value/tests/test_loaders.py` — Input loading, missing/malformed JSON handling.
- `skill/test-value/tests/test_aggregate_end_to_end.py` — Deterministic ordering, reconciled totals, both output artefacts.
- `docs/dev/test-value-skill-reference.md` — Decisions, definitions, limitations and reproducible-command reference.
- `README.md` — Register the new skill (if the repo lists skills there).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Dependency risk:** the mutation arm (`SA-0MV28WY5Q003N54O`) is planned, not
  landed. The aggregator can be built and unit-tested against synthetic mutation
  input, but should not be declared a complete per-file verdict until real mutation
  evidence exists; until then mutation is an honestly-absent signal.
- **Attribution risk:** mutation scores are per-module, so per-file attribution
  follows the suite→source map and is approximate. The report must caveat this
  rather than imply per-file precision.
- **Conservatism risk:** a `prune` verdict driven by a static anti-pattern could
  hide a genuinely valuable test. Mitigation: `prune` is advisory only, requires
  corroborating evidence (absent/weak mutation signal, not merely one static veto)
  and never deletes anything itself.
- **Scope-creep risk:** richer signal weighting, extra analysers (near-duplicate,
  assertion-quality) or automatic remediation must be filed as linked work items,
  not pulled into this item.
- **Assumption:** upstream analysers keep their current JSON schemas
  (`test_churn_data.json`, `evaluate_usefulness.py --json`, the planned
  `mutation_report.json` + `suite_source_map.json`). Schema drift is handled by an
  explicit loader error, not silent inference.

## Related work

- `SA-0MVSGIMHK004QHOO` — test-value refactor epic (classify/prove/report); this skill supplies the per-file reconciled register its Classify/Prove phases need.
- `SA-0MV28WY5Q003N54O` — mutation testing on top-churn modules (behavioural evidence arm; supplies mutation scores + suite→source map). **Blocker dependency:** the aggregator is most useful once mutation evidence exists; it can be planned but should not land before this arm.
- `skill/test-churn`, `skill/test/scripts/evaluate_usefulness.py`, `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md` — upstream signal sources.
- `SA-0MVXVC6C4009661D` — near-duplicate test detection (complementary cheap signal; potential future input).
- `SA-0MVXVC33N007Q71K` — assertion-quality / mock-density analyser (potential future input).
- `SA-0MVXVC9FM003ZJKJ` — per-test runtime and flakiness (the runtime/flake signal, may be absent).

# Intake Brief: Assertion-Quality and Mock-Density Analyser

**Work Item:** SA-0MVXVC33N007Q71K
**Issue Type:** feature
**Priority:** medium

## Headline

Add a static analyser that measures how well test files assert observable behaviour versus mocking internal collaborators, producing a per-file signal for the mutation-testing pre-filter pipeline.

## Problem statement

`evaluate_usefulness.py` detects crude anti-patterns (source-grep, placeholder, zero assertions, self-referential) but cannot distinguish a test that asserts observable behaviour from one that asserts internal collaborator calls, nor quantify mock density — a key variable in the hypothesis that mock-heavy suites detect fewer faults. Without this signal, the mutation campaign has no cheap way to pre-filter suites by assertion quality.

## Users

- **Mutation-testing pipeline** — needs a per-file signal (mock density, assertion quality) to prioritise which suites are worth mutating.
  - *User story:* "As the mutation-testing pipeline, I want a cheap static score for each test file so I can skip mock-heavy suites that are unlikely to yield mutations."
- **Test-suite maintainer / reviewer** — wants a signal that flags `toHaveBeenCalledWith`-heavy tests on internal collaborators, aligned with the calibration rules in SA-0MV28WX8Y005B05G.
  - *User story:* "As a test-suite maintainer, I want the analyser to flag mock-call assertions on internal collaborators so I can review whether they are boundary assertions or pinned wiring."
- **AI agent (implement)** — needs clear, conservative output with uncertainty reporting, not false positives.
  - *User story:* "As an AI agent evaluating test files, I want the analyser to report uncertainty rather than a definitive verdict when the signal is ambiguous."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **TypeScript/JavaScript test parsing** — The analyser parses `.test.ts`, `.spec.ts`, `.test.js`, `.spec.js` files and reports per file: total assertion count, count of assertions on internal collaborators vs public/behaviour, mock/stub/spy instantiation count and ratio, and number of test cases with no meaningful assertion.
2. **Mock-call flagging** — Assertions on `toHaveBeenCalledWith`, `toHaveBeenNthCalledWith`, `assert_called_once_with`, `mock.call_args_list` on internal collaborators are reported as a distinct, actionable signal (aligned with SA-0MV28WX8Y005B05G).
3. **Dual output** — The analyser emits both JSON (structured data for the pipeline) and Markdown (human-readable report) with documented definitions and conservative thresholds clearly stated.
4. **Uncertainty handling** — The analyser handles dynamic/indirect assertion styles (e.g., assertions via helper functions, parameterised tests, dynamic expect targets) without crashing, and reports uncertainty rather than a false verdict.
5. **Static pre-filter** — The analyser runs as a cheap pre-filter (no test execution, sub-second per file) and documents in its README that it is a proxy signal, not ground truth.
6. **Tests and documentation** — Covered by unit tests; all related documentation updated; full project test suite passes.

## Impact

As a test-suite maintainer, I can now pre-filter mock-heavy test suites before mutation testing and get a clear signal on tests that rely too heavily on `toHaveBeenCalledWith` assertions.

## Constraints

- Static analysis only; never executes the target project's tests.
- Conservative: uncertainty is reported, never auto-pruned or auto-flagged for removal.
- Language-neutral entry point with per-language adapters; no hardcoded project paths.
- TypeScript/JavaScript is the first-class target; Python is out of scope for v1 (marked as a future extension).

## Existing state

- `evaluate_usefulness.py` detects source-grep, placeholder, zero-assertion, self-referential, and duplicate-coverage anti-patterns via regex-based code-path analysis. It cannot quantify mock density or distinguish assertion types.
- `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md` documents test-quality standards including the mock-call assertion calibration.
- `SA-0MV28WX8Y005B05G` records the retain/migrate rule for `toHaveBeenCalledWith` on internal collaborators (148 retained, 7 migrated in the downtime-worker test file).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/test/scripts/assertion_quality_analyser.py` — New entry point / CLI script.
- `skill/test/scripts/assertion_quality_analyser/` — Per-language adapter packages (`typescript_adapter.py`, `python_adapter.py` stub).
- `skill/test/scripts/assertion_quality_analyser/models.py` — Data models for the output (assertion quality score, mock density ratio, etc.).
- `skill/test/scripts/assertion_quality_analyser/README.md` — Documentation with definitions, thresholds, and proxy-vs-ground-truth disclaimer.
- `skill/test/tests/test_assertion_quality_analyser.py` — Unit tests.

## Related work

- `SA-0MV28WX8Y005B05G` — Assert at the unit's observable contract: calibration for `toHaveBeenCalledWith` (call-argument assertion rules).
- `SA-0MVSGIMHK004QHOO` — Complete test-value refactor: ensure every test earns its runtime (epic umbrella).
- `SA-0MV28WY5Q003N54O` — Run mutation testing on top-churn modules to measure real test value (mutation testing, ground truth).
- `SA-0MVXVBZT7003VOCO` — Add a test-value aggregator skill combining churn, mutation and anti-pattern signals (consumes this analyser's output).
- `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md` — Test quality standards.
- `skill/test/scripts/evaluate_usefulness.py` — Existing anti-pattern detector (parent tool, not a replacement).

## Risks & Assumptions

| Risk / Assumption | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Distinguishing "internal collaborator" from "public behaviour" assertions requires understanding the production code's interface. Static analysis alone may be insufficient. | Report uncertainty when the classification is ambiguous. Flag all `toHaveBeenCalledWith`-style assertions and let the user decide; do not auto-classify. |
| Mock density threshold is subjective. | Document the threshold as a configurable constant with a clear rationale. Default to a conservative value. |
| Adding Python parsing increases scope beyond the stated v1 target. | Lock Python to "future extension" in the description. Implement only TypeScript/JavaScript adapters for v1. |
| The aggregator (`SA-0MVXVBZT7003VOCO`) may need a different output format. | Design the JSON output with an open schema; the aggregator can adapt. Document the schema version. |
| Scope creep: the analyser could expand into a full test-quality tool. | The README explicitly states this is a pre-filter proxy, not a replacement for mutation testing or manual review. |

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Should Python test parsing be included in v1 or deferred?" — Answer (Map, intake draft): Deferred to a future extension. TypeScript/JavaScript is the v1 target. Rationale: the mutation-testing pipeline currently operates on TS/JS code; adding Python doubles the adapter scope without proportional benefit. Source: intake draft authoring decision.
- Q: "What constitutes 'internal collaborator' for static analysis?" — Answer (Map, intake draft): A mock/stub/spy that is injected or provided as a dependency within the test file's module scope, as opposed to a framework-level assertion on the return value of a production function call. Static analysis classifies by import/dependency pattern; ambiguous cases are flagged as uncertain. Source: intake draft authoring decision.

# Add near-duplicate test detection to find redundant test coverage

## Goal

As a maintainer of a large test suite, I want the test-value tooling to report
near-duplicate test blocks and files, so additive accumulation can be measured
and redundant coverage pruned with evidence instead of suspicion.

## Problem statement

The test-churn analysis measured large net test growth (+137,022 lines, +384
files on the reference project) against a **low** rewrite ratio (14.0%
modified-only), so the suite grows by *additive accumulation*, not churn. The
only existing redundancy check — `skill/test/scripts/evaluate_usefulness.py`'s
"duplicate coverage" veto — matches test *names* containing `again|also covers|
duplicate|already covered` inside a single file. It cannot see a copy-pasted
test with renamed identifiers, nor the same behaviour re-tested through a
different import path, so redundancy accumulates with nothing forcing a
re-examination.

## Users

- **Producer / engineering manager** — wants the *size* of the redundancy, not
  just total growth, to decide whether pruning is worth runtime.
- **Implementer of the test-value refactor epic** (`SA-0MVSGIMHK004QHOO`) —
  needs block-level, line-range evidence for the Classify and Prove steps; the
  epic's AC3 forbids deleting a test on suspicion alone.
- **Agent working a prune pass** — needs a deterministic, read-only command
  whose JSON can be joined with churn and usefulness data.

Example user stories:

- As a producer, I want a ranked list of duplicate test clusters with redundant
  line counts so I can see how much of the growth is redundancy.
- As the refactor implementer, I want each cluster to name the file and line
  range of every member so a prune candidate can be proven, not guessed.
- As an agent, I want `expected-repetition` (parametrised/table-driven cases)
  excluded by the tool so I do not file bogus prune items.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1 — **Detection is structural, not textual.** Near-duplicate test blocks are detected within and across files using normalised representation: Python test blocks via `ast` (docstrings stripped, identifiers replaced by positional placeholders, literals canonicalised to type placeholders so a renamed copy still matches), JavaScript/TypeScript/other test files via comment-stripped token normalisation with brace-matched block boundaries. Raw text equality is never the similarity measure.
- [ ] AC2 — **Clusters are reported with location and score.** Each cluster lists every member's file path, start–end line range, block size (lines and tokens), member-to-member and cluster similarity score, and a redundancy measure (member lines minus the largest member's lines) used to order the report. Both `test_duplicates.json` (versioned schema: thresholds, method, limitations, clusters) and `test_duplicate_report.md` (human, same content, ordered by redundancy) are written to `--output-dir`.
- [ ] AC3 — **Conservatism and legitimate repetition.** Parametrised/table-driven repetition is classified `expected-repetition`, not redundancy: `pytest.mark.parametrize`, `unittest.subTest`, `test.each`/`it.each`, and blocks whose sweep is a data loop over case literals are detected and excluded. Similarity bands are explicit (`duplicate` ≥ threshold, default 0.85; `near-duplicate` between the lower band, default 0.65, and the threshold), every cluster carries a `report-only` verdict, and the tool never edits, deletes or renames anything.
- [ ] AC4 — **Performance is bounded and documented.** Defaults skip trivial blocks (`--min-lines`, default 10) and bound the candidate set; comparison uses an inverted shingle index plus optional MinHash banding rather than all-pairs O(n²). Scope options `--changed-only <base-ref>` (git diff), `--max-files N`, `--min-lines N`, `--threshold` and `--min-shared-tokens` are documented with the complexity they imply, and a measured runtime figure for a ~500-test-file suite is recorded in the docs and in the report preamble.
- [ ] AC5 — **Behaviour is pinned by tests.** Unit tests cover: normalisation invariance (a copy with renamed identifiers still scores ≥ threshold), distinct behaviour staying below the band, `expected-repetition` exclusion for parametrised and table-driven cases, threshold boundary behaviour, cluster ordering and redundant-line arithmetic, JSON and Markdown schema/content, an empty or single-block suite, a non-Python file set, and one end-to-end run over a fixture suite. Every test asserts one documented behaviour and no test re-implements the similarity algorithm under test.
- [ ] AC6 — **Documentation is updated.** `skill/test-churn/SKILL.md` gains a "Near-duplicate detection" section wired into the existing pruning workflow (step 2 "inspect candidates" gains the command as the evidence source for the duplicate-coverage bullet); `docs/dev/test-churn-skill-reference.md` records the method, thresholds, complexity/runtime bound, worked example and limitations; the `README.md` skill line mentions it; and the docs state that this analyser supersedes `evaluate_usefulness.py`'s name-marker heuristic for near-duplicates. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] AC7 — **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Impact

A maintainer can see — ranked by redundant line count — exactly which test
blocks duplicate each other and prune them on recorded evidence, instead of
inferring redundancy from a raw growth number.

## Constraints

- **Read-only.** No automatic deletion, editing or renaming of test files; no
  writes outside `--output-dir`.
- **Conservative thresholds.** A false "duplicate" verdict is worse than a
  miss: uncertainty reports, never removes.
- **No hardcoded project paths.** Test/source classification and language
  handling follow the configurable, language-neutral approach already used by
  `ChurnConfig`; extend it rather than forking it.
- **Python standard library only.** The repository has zero third-party
  dependencies (`package.json` `dependencies: {}`, no `requirements.txt`); no
  tree-sitter/esprima/acorn dependency may be added.
- **No network, no per-block subprocess.** The analyser must not shell out to
  `node`, `pytest` or a language server; all parsing is in-process.
- **Deterministic output.** Same tree and flags ⇒ byte-identical JSON, so
  results are comparable over time (the churn analyser's existing property).

## Existing state

- `skill/test-churn/scripts/test_churn_analysis.py` (1,586 lines) — history-based
  churn: `ChurnConfig`, `is_test_file`, `classify_area`, `build_report`,
  `write_outputs`, CLI (`--project-root --branch --since --max-commits
  --output-dir --config --format --stdout --quiet`). It measures *how test code
  changes over time*; it contains no similarity analysis and never reads test
  bodies.
- `skill/test/scripts/evaluate_usefulness.py` (279 lines) — per-file verdicts.
  `_detect_duplicate` is a name-marker regex plus "imports production code";
  `VERDICT_REPORT` is always used for duplicate-only findings.
- `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md` — anti-pattern 4 "duplicates of
  existing core coverage" (same behaviour via a different import path) is prose
  with no automated check; the churn skill's pruning workflow names it but
  offers only a manual grep.
- `skill/shared/tree_coverage.py::jaccard_similarity` — word-token Jaccard over
  *text* strings; precedent for the metric, unusable for code ASTs (no
  normalisation, no block boundaries).
- `skill/test-churn/tests/` — `conftest.py` loads the analyser by path
  (`test_churn_analysis_under_test`) so it is not collected as a test module;
  `.pi/test-config.json` has no `test-churn` group, so these tests currently run
  only under `full`.

## Desired change

A new read-only analyser `skill/test-churn/scripts/test_duplicate_detection.py`
with a CLI shaped like its churn sibling:

1. **Collect** test files using the existing classification (`is_test_file` +
   `ChurnConfig`), honouring `--changed-only <base-ref>` / `--max-files`.
2. **Extract blocks** with file + line range: Python via `ast` (top-level
   functions/classes/methods plus `with`-wrapped test bodies), JS/TS and other
   languages via comment-stripped tokenisation with brace/paren matching. Blocks
   smaller than `--min-lines` are skipped.
3. **Normalise** (docstrings and comments dropped, identifiers mapped to
   positional placeholders per scope, literals canonicalised by type, whitespace
   collapsed) so renamed copies remain identical while different behaviour does
   not.
4. **Fingerprint and compare**: token k-gram shingles (k default 5) → Jaccard
   similarity; candidates from an inverted shingle index (optionally MinHash
   banding) instead of all pairs; file-level rollup reports the strongest block
   pair per file pair.
5. **Classify** each pair as `duplicate`, `near-duplicate` or
   `expected-repetition` (parametrisation/data-loop detection), then cluster
   transitively and order clusters by redundant lines.
6. **Write** `test_duplicate_report.md` + `test_duplicates.json` with method,
   thresholds, limitations and measured runtime in the preamble; print a
   one-line summary to stderr.

The script is wired into the churn skill's pruning workflow and reference docs;
`evaluate_usefulness.py` keeps its heuristic unchanged (it answers a different,
per-file question) but its duplicate-coverage reason cross-references the new
tool.

## Key Files

- `skill/test-churn/scripts/test_duplicate_detection.py` — **new** analyser: block extraction, normalisation, shingling/Jaccard, clustering, JSON + Markdown writers, CLI.
- `skill/test-churn/scripts/test_churn_analysis.py` — reuse `ChurnConfig`/`is_test_file`/`classify_area`; factor any shared helpers rather than duplicating them (no behaviour change to existing metrics).
- `skill/test-churn/tests/test_test_duplicate_detection.py` — **new** unit + end-to-end suite for the analyser.
- `skill/test-churn/tests/conftest.py` — add a path-loaded fixture for the new module (same pattern as `churn`).
- `skill/test-churn/SKILL.md` — new "Near-duplicate detection" section; pruning-workflow step 2 gains the command.
- `docs/dev/test-churn-skill-reference.md` — method, thresholds, complexity/runtime bound, worked example, limitations.
- `README.md` — extend the test-churn bullet to name near-duplicate detection.
- `skill/test/scripts/evaluate_usefulness.py` — docstring/reason cross-reference to the new tool (no behaviour change).
- `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md` — anti-pattern 4 gains the automated-evidence pointer.
- `.pi/test-config.json` — optional: add a `test-churn` group (`skill/test-churn/**`) so changed-scope runs execute these tests instead of falling through to `full`.

## Risks and assumptions

- **False-positive duplicates** (shared boilerplate, fixture setup, mechanical
  parameter sweeps) are the dominant risk and the reason for report-only
  verdicts: mitigation is the `expected-repetition` classifier, a conservative
  default threshold of 0.85 with a separate `near-duplicate` band, `--min-lines`
  skipping trivial blocks, and a documented limitations section.
- **Parser fragility outside Python** — brace matching on JS/TS is approximate;
  mitigation is conservative fallback (a block that cannot be delimited is
  reported as "unparsed" in the JSON summary rather than silently compared as a
  whole file), plus a non-Python fixture in the tests.
- **Performance on large suites** — shingle construction is linear in tokens,
  but candidate pairing can still blow up; mitigation is the inverted index,
  `--max-files`/`--changed-only` scope options and a measured runtime figure
  recorded in the docs.
- **Scope creep** — "also fix the duplicated tests" is explicitly out of scope:
  remediation belongs to the epic's prune/rework children. Any duplication the
  tool finds in this repository is reported as evidence in a comment or a
  follow-on item, not fixed here.
- **Assumption A1** — the detector belongs beside the churn analyser in
  `skill/test-churn/` rather than inside `evaluate_usefulness.py`, because it is
  suite-wide measurement, not a per-file verdict, and the churn skill is where
  the pruning workflow lives.
- **Assumption A2** — no new third-party parser dependency (stdlib only), so
  JS/TS detection is token-based rather than AST-based; Python gets exact AST
  normalisation.
- **Assumption A3** — the item stays `discovered-from:SA-0MV28WY5Q003N54O`
  rather than being re-parented under `SA-0MVSGIMHK004QHOO`; the epic's
  Classify/Prove children consume its output, and re-parenting a
  `plan_complete` epic would change that epic's scope.
- **Assumption A4** — a `test-churn` test group does not exist in
  `.pi/test-config.json` today; adding one is a small, separable improvement
  that keeps these tests out of the `full`-only path (optional within this
  item).

## Related work

- `SA-0MVSGIMHK004QHOO` — test-value refactor epic; additive accumulation is its
  stated failure mode and this analyser feeds its Classify and Prove steps.
- `SA-0MV28WY5Q003N54O` — mutation testing; a direct fault-detection signal that
  complements this cheap redundancy signal (discovery source for this item).
- `SA-0MV28WX8Y005B05G` — prefer interface/behaviour assertions over
  `toHaveBeenCalledWith`; overlapping "rework" direction, different evidence.
- `SA-0MVSCZ2U500420IC` — integrate test-churn metrics into the refactor skill:
  a natural consumer of this output.
- Code: `skill/test-churn/scripts/test_churn_analysis.py`,
  `skill/test/scripts/evaluate_usefulness.py`,
  `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md` (anti-pattern 4),
  `docs/dev/test-churn-skill-reference.md`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Duplicate-work check performed with `wl search` over "duplicate test", "clone
detection", "test redundancy" and "near-duplicate … coverage" — no completed or
open item overlaps these acceptance criteria (the nearest hits are intake
duplicate-work detection `SA-0MTWMCJ37000485M` and the refactor skill's
`consolidate_duplicates.py`, both different problems: work-item duplication and
duplicated *work items*, not duplicated test blocks).

No interactive interview round was held: the seed description already carried a
problem statement, six acceptance criteria, constraints and related work, so the
intake was driven by repository research instead of questions. The four open
design decisions were resolved as documented assumptions for review:

- Q: "Where should the near-duplicate detector live — extend
  `evaluate_usefulness.py`, or a new script beside the churn analyser?" —
  **Answer (agent assumption A1, pending producer confirmation):** new script
  `skill/test-churn/scripts/test_duplicate_detection.py`. Research: inspected
  `skill/test/scripts/evaluate_usefulness.py` (per-file verdict, name-marker
  duplicate heuristic) and `skill/test-churn/scripts/test_churn_analysis.py`
  (suite-wide measurement, `ChurnConfig`, report writers); the new capability is
  suite-wide, so it follows the churn analyser's shape. Source: repository
  inspection.
- Q: "May a parser dependency (tree-sitter/esprima) be added for exact JS/TS
  ASTs?" — **Answer (agent assumption A2, pending producer confirmation):** no.
  Research: the repository carries zero third-party dependencies
  (`package.json` `dependencies: {}`, no `requirements.txt`), so JS/TS detection
  uses token normalisation and Python uses stdlib `ast`. Source: repository
  inspection.
- Q: "Should this item be re-parented under the test-value epic?" — **Answer
  (agent assumption A3, pending producer confirmation):** no; keep
  `discovered-from:SA-0MV28WY5Q003N54O` and cross-reference the epic, whose
  Classify/Prove children consume the output. Source: `wl show
  SA-0MVSGIMHK004QHOO --json`.
- Q: "Is a `test-churn` test group worth adding so these tests run on
  changed-scope gates?" — **Answer (agent assumption A4, optional within this
  item):** yes if it stays a one-line config addition; `.pi/test-config.json`
  currently has no group covering `skill/test-churn/**`. Source: repository
  inspection.

# Intake Brief: Repeat producer actions in red on the final report conclusion

## Problem statement

The canonical end-of-session report (`skill/report`) lists blocking producer
actions in `## Producer Actions`, but the `## Conclusion` — the last thing the
operator reads — does not repeat them. When a session ends with something the
producer must do (answer a question, make a decision, grant an approval), the
operator can miss it in the body of a long report. Repeating any genuine
producer action in the Conclusion in red makes the blocking call-to-action
impossible to overlook.

## Users

- **Producer/operator** reading end-of-session reports in the pi TUI: wants the
  blocking action to stand out at the end of the report, not be buried mid-page.
- **Agent (intake/plan/implement/audit/…) authoring the report**: keeps passing
  blocking actions via `--producer-actions`; the renderer handles the red
  repetition deterministically (no per-skill change).

Example user stories:

- "As a producer, when a skill session needs a decision from me, I want that
  decision repeated in red in the conclusion so I cannot miss it."
- "As a producer, when nothing is required of me, I do not want a red warning in
  the conclusion."
- "As an agent, I want the renderer to do this automatically so every skill
  behaves the same way."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When the normalised producer actions are a genuine, non-`None needed`
   action, `render_report()` appends the action text **verbatim** to the
   `## Conclusion` section, wrapped in ANSI SGR red (`\x1b[31m…\x1b[0m`) with a
   `⚠️ Producer action required:` lead-in. Verified by unit test asserting the
   escape sequences and the exact action text inside `## Conclusion`.
2. When no producer actions are supplied, or the supplied text is routine
   workflow progression that normalises to `None needed`, the Conclusion
   contains no ANSI escape sequences and no repeated action text. Verified by
   unit tests (absent actions; `Proceed to /skill:plan`; `Review the brief, then
   run /skill:plan`).
3. Colour can be disabled with a new `--no-colour` CLI flag **or** the standard
   `NO_COLOR` environment variable (non-empty). In that mode the Conclusion
   still repeats the action in plain text with the `⚠️` marker and contains no
   ANSI escape sequences. Verified by unit tests for both opt-outs.
4. Multi-line / multi-action producer text is repeated verbatim (line breaks
   preserved) and the rest of the report is unchanged: section order,
   `## Producer Actions` → `## Notes` → `## Conclusion`, the existing
   completed/incomplete conclusion sentences, and the `</end_session>`
   terminator. Verified by regression tests.
5. `skill/report/SKILL.md` documents the conditional red repetition in the
   canonical template, the layout rules, and the colour opt-out
   (`--no-colour` / `NO_COLOR`) alongside the existing icon opt-out. Verified
   by document review.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Implement in the shared renderer only (`skill/report/scripts/render_report.py`)
  plus a small shared colour helper — do not fork report logic into the ~17
  calling skills.
- Repeat **after** routine-next-step normalisation (SA-0MVNQ3RLW006XEFW): a
  routine next step must never produce red text.
- Do not use TTY detection to decide colour: the CLI's stdout is captured/piped
  by agents before being pasted into the final response, so TTY detection would
  disable the feature exactly where it is needed. Opt-out must be explicit
  (`--no-colour` / `NO_COLOR`).
- Colour is decorative: the `⚠️` marker and the plain action text must carry the
  meaning when colour is unavailable, so the report stays readable in
  non-ANSI consumers (GitHub, plain-text logs).
- No new runtime dependency; pure-Python, offline-testable.
- Do not change `## Producer Actions` semantics, the pane-status derivation, or
  the existing conclusion wording.

## Existing state

- `render_report()` renders `## Producer Actions` from the normalised
  `producer_actions` string (`None needed` when absent), then `## Notes`, then
  `## Conclusion`.
- The Conclusion currently emits one of two fixed sentences based on AC
  verdicts (`_derive_session_status`): completed → "This completes … Ready for
  `<next_action>`."; incomplete → "… is incomplete. Requires attention
  (`<next_action>`)." Nothing else is appended.
- `skill/shared/herdr_pane.py` already provides `icons_enabled(no_icons, env)`
  honouring `--no-icons` / `WL_NO_ICONS=1` — the convention to mirror for
  colour, but colour must be a separate switch (`WL_NO_ICONS` must not disable
  colour).
- No ANSI/colour handling exists anywhere in the report renderer today (the
  only ANSI in the repo is in `tests/integration/test-worktree-workflow.sh`).

## Desired change

- Add `colour_enabled(no_colour=False, env=None)` (and `RED`/`RESET` constants)
  to `skill/shared/herdr_pane.py`: enabled by default; disabled by
  `--no-colour` or a non-empty `NO_COLOR`.
- In `render_report()`, after the existing conclusion sentence(s), when the
  normalised producer actions are not `None needed`, append a blank line and a
  red line: `⚠️ Producer action required: <verbatim action text>`. Apply
  `RED … RESET` only when colour is enabled.
- Thread an optional `no_colour: bool = False` parameter through
  `render_report()`, `render_report_from_workitem()`, `render_from_wl()` and the
  CLI, adding the `--no-colour` flag.
- Update `skill/report/SKILL.md` (template, layout rules, example, colour
  opt-out) and the `README.md` report-helper bullet to mention the red
  repetition.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/report/scripts/render_report.py` — conditional red repetition in the
  Conclusion; `no_colour` plumbing and `--no-colour` flag.
- `skill/shared/herdr_pane.py` — `colour_enabled()` helper + `RED`/`RESET`
  constants mirroring `icons_enabled()`.
- `skill/report/tests/test_render_report.py` — new tests: red repetition,
  no-repetition for absent/routine actions, `--no-colour`/`NO_COLOR` fallback,
  multi-line preservation, structure regression.
- `skill/shared/tests/test_herdr_pane.py` — `colour_enabled()` unit tests.
- `skill/report/SKILL.md` — template/layout/example + colour opt-out docs.
- `README.md` — report-helper bullet: note the red repetition of blocking
  producer actions in the Conclusion.

## Related work

- **SA-0MVNQ3RLW006XEFW** — "Don't include producer actions that are next steps"
  (completed): established normalisation to `None needed`; the red repetition
  must run after it.
- **SA-0MULPQ3BK001A1M5** — "Misleading completion message on LLM summaries"
  (completed): made the Conclusion reflect session status; this item extends the
  same section.
- **SA-0MTFLQEQQ0083EW1** — "Update pane title with status emoticon on skill
  completion" (completed): established the ✅/⚠️/🚫 status colour semantics this
  feature reuses for a red call-to-action.
- **SA-0MSJ082OY003IQ8S** — "Standardize skill session end-of-session reporting
  via helper report skill" (completed): origin of the canonical report contract.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — "red font" means ANSI SGR red in terminal output.** The report
  is rendered to stdout and pasted into the pi TUI; ANSI is the only mechanism
  that reliably colours that path. If the producer expects Markdown/HTML
  colouring, the brief should be revised before implementation (documented in
  the Appendix).
- **Assumption — red repeats blocking actions only.** Because routine workflow
  progression is normalised to `None needed` first, it can never trigger red;
  this avoids the false "producer is blocking" signal fixed by
  SA-0MVNQ3RLW006XEFW.
- **Assumption — no TTY detection.** Explicit opt-out only, because agent-captured
  stdout is not a TTY.
- **Risk — ANSI leakage into non-terminal consumers** (GitHub, PRs, plain logs).
  Mitigation: `--no-colour`/`NO_COLOR`, plus the `⚠️` marker and plain text so the
  meaning survives even if escapes are stripped or shown literally.
- **Risk — colour-blindness / theme contrast.** Mitigation: the `⚠️` marker and
  the words "Producer action required" carry the signal; colour is decorative.
- **Risk — multi-line producer text.** Mitigation: wrap the whole block once and
  test line-break preservation rather than prefixing each line.
- **Scope creep.** Adjacent ideas (colouring the `## Producer Actions` section,
  colourising AC verdicts, HTML-export colour) are out of scope — record as
  separate work items.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "What does 'red font' mean for a Markdown report rendered by the LLM/TUI —
  ANSI escape codes, HTML `<span style=\"color:red\">`, or plain emphasis?"
  — **Answer (repo research + design analysis):** ANSI SGR red. The report is
  printed to stdout and pasted into the terminal-rendered TUI; raw ANSI passes
  through and colours the terminal, whereas inline HTML styles are not honoured
  by the Markdown→terminal path and GitHub strips `style` attributes. Recorded
  as an assumption; the producer can request an HTML/bold variant at review.
  No interactive round was required for the rest of the brief.
- Q: "Should routine next-step actions (e.g. 'Proceed to /skill:plan') also be
  repeated in red?" — **Answer (SA-0MVNQ3RLW006XEFW contract):** No. Routine
  workflow progression is normalised to `None needed` and must never be shown as
  a blocking red action; only genuine, current-stage actions are repeated.
- Q: "Should colour be auto-detected (TTY) or explicitly opt-out?" — **Answer
  (design analysis):** Explicit opt-out only. Agent-captured stdout is not a
  TTY, so TTY detection would silently disable the feature on the exact path
  that needs it. `--no-colour` and `NO_COLOR` are the opt-outs.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MVQ1QM9L0083KAW** – Producer Actions contract: docs and skill templates (completed)
- **SA-0MVNQ3RLW006XEFW** – Don't include producer actions that are next steps (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: action, actions, conclusion, final, llm, producer, red, repeat, them, there
- `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` — matched: action, actions, final, llm, output, producer, red, repeat, them, there
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — matched: action, actions, final, llm, output, producer, red, repeat, them, there

## Goal

`_git_commit_evidence` in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` resolves a
stranded child's pushed-commit evidence with
`git log <ref> --grep <child_id> -n 1`. `--grep` matches the **whole commit
message including the body**, so a commit that merely *mentions* a work-item id
counts as that item's work.

Observed 2026-11-01 during the epic drive for SA-0MVX1M6HH004YPX2: driven child
SA-0MVX359B7008R9F3 timed out after 3600 s with its own commit (`9119e4117`)
still unpushed in its worktree, and `drive` reported it as *stranded* with
evidence `0fb0e4305` — the **sibling** child's (SA-0MVX31GLC002IPR8) commit,
whose body names SA-0MVX359B7008R9F3 as the future home of the detection
module. The verdict told the operator to `--finalise-stranded` a child whose
work had never been pushed.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Commit evidence matches only commits whose **subject** references the
   work-item id, never a body-only mention.
2. A regression test pins the false-positive: a commit whose body mentions
   another item's id is not evidence for that item.
3. A driven child whose commit is still only in its own worktree is reported
   as non-terminal-with-work, not as stranded on the parent branch.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_git_commit_evidence`
- `skill/implement/tests/` — regression test

# Intake brief — re-filed from OSL-0MVXZOWSL007VREJ (ContentCreator worklog)

**Headline:** Add a consumption mechanism to the refactor skill so that `# <!-- REFACTOR-<id> ... -->` marker blocks are automatically detected as stale and flagged (or removed) when their recorded smell is fixed.

## Problem statement

The refactor skill injects `# <!-- REFACTOR-<work-item-id> ... -->` blocks into source files to record code smells. The expectation is that whoever fixes the smell also deletes the block. Nothing checks that this happened. Three stale blocks were found in a single sweep, and one live marker remains — proving the gap is ongoing, not a one-off.

## Users

- **Maintainer opening a file.** A stale marker asserts a live smell; disproving it requires a worklog lookup and wastes time.
- **The refactor skill itself (next run).** A stale block reads as a live smell and invites a duplicate work item.
- **The operator running periodic sweeps.** Currently they must manually delete each stale block (OSL-0MVVF1OAO007HIXW).

**User story:** "As a developer running the refactor skill or reading a file, I want stale REFACTOR markers to be flagged or removed automatically, so that the tree only contains markers for unfinished work."

## Existing state (verified during intake)

- The refactor skill writes markers via `comment_injection.py`; no corresponding consumption code exists.
- Markers contain: `REFACTOR-<id>`, `smell: <type>`, `severity: <level>`, `description: <text>`, and optionally `# status: resolved — <reason>`.
- OSL-0MVVF1OAO007HIXW removed three stale blocks by hand (completed). The consumption gap was recorded as this item (discovered-from:OSL-0MVVF1OAO007HIXW).
- One live marker remains in `tests/test_rss_freshness.py:2` (OSL-0MVY7WI0K009WE4L, ruff C408) — this is correct and should stay until the smell is fixed.
- The `# status: resolved` line exists in at least one marker (`scripts/tidy_residual_links.py`) but is not parsed by any tool.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The refactor skill exposes a reusable function `reap_stale_markers()` (or similar) that scans files for `# <!-- REFACTOR-... -->` blocks and returns a list of stale markers — each entry identifying the file path, line range, work item ID, and the reason the marker is stale (work item terminal / `# status: resolved` present / work item missing).
2. A new CLI entry point `python3 -m skill.refactor.scripts.reap_stale_markers` invokes the function, prints a summary of stale markers found, and exits non-zero if any are discovered — suitable for pre-commit or CI.
3. When invoked with `--dry-run` (default), the tool reports stale markers without modifying files; when invoked with `--remove`, it deletes the marker blocks in-place and preserves all other file content exactly.
4. The function correctly classifies a marker as stale when: (a) the referenced work item's status is `completed` or `deleted` (soft-deleted), or (b) the marker block itself contains `# status: resolved`, or (c) the referenced work item cannot be found (missing or inaccessible) — reason `work-item-missing`. It must NOT flag a marker as stale if the smell is still unfixed (work item is `open` and no resolved line).
5. `python3 -m ruff check` stays clean over all affected files; no `noqa` or config suppression is added.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (`./scripts/run_tests.sh`).

## Constraints

- Keep it out of `comment_injection.py` — that mechanism is correct; the gap is consumption.
- The tool must work with the Worklog CLI (`wl show --json`) to check item status; do not add a direct database dependency.
- Do not modify marker copies inside `.worklog/worktrees/*` — only process files in the source tree.
- The `# status: resolved` line format is `# status: resolved — <reason>`; parse this conservatively (presence of `status: resolved` is sufficient).
- If a marker references a work item that cannot be found (item does not exist or is inaccessible), treat it as stale with reason `work-item-missing`.

## Desired change

Add a new module `refactor/reap_markers.py` (or `refactor/consumption.py`) with the detection logic, a CLI entry point, and tests. The refactor skill's main scan should optionally invoke this as a pre-flight or post-flight check.

## Key Files

- `skill/refactor/comment_injection.py` — reference only; own the marker format, do not modify
- `skill/refactor/workitem_creation.py` — reference only; understand `REFACTOR_PATTERN` matching
- `skill/refactor/reap_markers.py` — new module: detection logic + public API (`reap_stale_markers()`)
- `skill/refactor/scripts/reap_stale_markers.py` — new CLI entry point
- `skill/refactor/SKILL.md` — document the reaper and its place in the scan lifecycle
- `tests/test_refactor/test_reap_markers.py` — new test file (mirrors `tests/test_refactor/test_comment_injection.py`)

## Related work

- `OSL-0MVVF1OAO007HIXW` — Remove stale REFACTOR- marker blocks left in tests and scripts (completed) — manual sweep of three blocks
- `OSL-0MVY7WI0K009WE4L` — Live marker in `tests/test_rss_freshness.py` (ruff C408) — should remain until fixed
- `OSL-0MVM96NMG002ZAMZ` — Recover orphaned refactor-batch edits (completed) — same marker mechanism, different problem
- `OSL-0MVVE7V84007DQD0` — Marker-above-shebang near miss (completed) — edge case for comment placement

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** the Worklog CLI (`wl show`) is available and reliable for checking item status during the refactor skill's run. **Mitigation:** handle CLI errors gracefully (treat unreachable items as potentially stale with a warning).
- **Risk — false positive:** a marker could reference a completed item that is still relevant as historical context. **Mitigation:** default to `--dry-run` mode; require explicit `--remove` to delete.
- **Risk — scope creep:** turning this into a full repo-wide cleanup sweep. **Mitigation:** scope is the detection/reporting mechanism only; bulk removal is a separate concern.
- **Assumption:** `# status: resolved` is the canonical in-marker resolution signal. **Mitigation:** documented in the new module's docstring; the operator can update if the convention changes.

## Appendix: clarifying questions and answers

No interview round was run: the problem, scope, constraints, and related work were answerable by repo and worklog search.

- **Q (resolved by search):** What markers currently exist in the repo? — **Answer:** one live marker in `tests/test_rss_freshness.py:2` (OSL-0MVY7WI0K009WE4L, ruff C408, smell still unfixed) and three stale markers that were deleted by OSL-0MVVF1OAO007HIXW. Source: grep, this session.
- **Q (resolved by search):** Is `# status: resolved` a real convention or just an ad-hoc line? — **Answer:** it appears on at least one marker (`scripts/tidy_residual_links.py`) and was noted in the OSL-0MVVF1OAO007HIXW implementation report as evidence the smell was fixed. It is a convention worth formalising in the reap module. Source: `wl show OSL-0MVM4UWDI001GZNY`, this session.
- **Q (resolved by search):** Can the refactor skill invoke `wl`? — **Answer:** yes — the refactor skill's scripts already use the Worklog CLI (e.g., `wl list --tags Refactor`). Source: inspection of `comment_injection.py`, `workitem_creation.py`, this session.
- **Duplicate check:** `wl search "REFACTOR marker reap consumption stale"` returned only OSL-0MVXZOWSL007VREJ itself and OSL-0MVVF1OAO007HIXW (the manual sweep). No item covers automated consumption.

## Appendix: plan-session questions (plan skill)

Planning stopped at the interview step: the item cannot be decomposed into
implementation tasks until repository ownership is settled.

- **OPEN QUESTION (blocking; directed to the producer):** Which repository
  should the reap implementation land in? The item's ACs and Key Files target
  the shared/global refactor skill (AC1 "The refactor skill exposes a reusable
  function", Key Files `.pi/agent/skills/refactor/...`, AC2
  `python3 -m refactor.reap`), but that skill is developed in the **SorraAgents**
  repository (`skill/refactor/`, installed as the symlink
  `~/.pi/agent/skills -> ~/projects/SorraAgents/skill`) and every refactor-skill
  change is tracked there under SA- IDs (e.g. SA-0MVPUVM8F006270F,
  SA-0MVGKMNEQ009RZKD). This item is filed in the **ContentCreator** worklog
  (OSL-). **Why it matters:** it decides which repo the code, tests and commits
  go into, and the implement skill's worktree isolation normally forbids
  editing outside the ContentCreator worktree.
  - Options: **(a)** re-file as an SA- item in the SorraAgents worklog and
    redirect/close this OSL item — *recommended*, matches every other
    refactor-skill change; **(b)** keep the OSL item and author cross-repo
    changes into SorraAgents from it — needs explicit authorisation;
    **(c)** rescope this OSL item to a ContentCreator-local reap tool (e.g.
    `scripts/reap_stale_markers.py` over ContentCreator's own tree) and relax
    AC1's skill wording.
  - Evidence gathered: `git ls-files | grep refactor` in ContentCreator returns
    0 paths; `.pi/agent/` does not exist in ContentCreator;
    `.pi/skills_extensions/` supports only `SKILL_PREFIX.md` / `SKILL_POSTFIX.md`
    / `extension.json` (prose and data, not Python modules).
  - **Preferred option: (a).**
  - **ANSWER (producer, this session): (a)** — re-file as an SA- item in the
    SorraAgents worklog and redirect this OSL item. FINAL. That re-filing is
    this work item; `OSL-0MVXZOWSL007VREJ` was deleted after it was created.
- **Q (resolved by inspection, no operator input needed):** Where are the live
  REFACTOR markers today? — **Answer:** two. `tests/test_rss_freshness.py:1`
  (OSL-0MVY7WI0K009WE4L, `complexity`, C408, item `open` — correctly *not*
  stale) and `tests/test_rss_regenerate.py:1` (OSL-0MVYHBV60007WKHK,
  `ruff_specific`, RUF059, item `open` — also not stale). Source: grep over
  the ContentCreator tree, this session. Note the second marker's work item
  records a *worktree* path (`<main>/.worklog/worktrees/<wt>`),
  which is relevant to the "do not modify marker copies inside
  `.worklog/worktrees/*`" constraint.
- **Q (resolved by inspection):** Does the marker format match what
  `comment_injection.py` writes? — **Answer:** yes — `# <!-- REFACTOR-<id>`,
  `# smell:`, `# severity:`, `# description:`, `# -->`. The optional
  `# status: resolved — <reason>` line is *not* produced by
  `_build_comment_block()`; it is added by hand, so the reap module must treat
  it as an optional extra line inside the block.

## Re-filing record

Re-filed from `OSL-0MVXZOWSL007VREJ` in the ContentCreator worklog. The producer
chose option (a): the reap implementation belongs to this repository, because
the refactor skill is developed here (`skill/refactor/`) and every
refactor-skill change is tracked under an SA- ID. The ContentCreator item was
deleted after this item was created.

Consequences applied to this brief:

- **Key Files** rewritten from the ContentCreator-relative
  `.pi/agent/skills/refactor/...` (which does not exist there) to this
  repository's real layout, and `skill/refactor/SKILL.md` added.
- **AC2** now names `python3 -m skill.refactor.scripts.reap_stale_markers`,
  matching this repository's invocation convention.
- **AC7** names the suite invocation (`./scripts/run_tests.sh`).

Planning status carried over from the ContentCreator session: the effort/risk
pre-check returned **skip** (Small / Low), the six automated review stages ran
against the brief, one unambiguous AC gap was closed (AC1/AC4 now include the
`work-item-missing` case that the Constraints already required), and the
acceptance-criteria coverage review returned **proceed**.
